note: This skill encodes a verification methodology, not jurisdiction-specific legal facts. Claims below are about the method and the authoritative professional/regulatory standards it aligns to, plus the local script self-check. No live document review was performed. The core discipline is anti-fabrication: a citation is never treated as proof of support.

claims.claim: A citation alone does not verify a claim; verification requires confirming the cited source actually supports the claim. Grading distinguishes Supported / Partial / Unsupported / Unverifiable / Misquoted.
claims.raw_snippet: Grade support by reading the source. No source access -> Unverifiable, never Supported. When unsure between two grades, grade DOWN.

claims.claim: Lawyers have a professional duty of candor toward the tribunal (not to knowingly make false statements of fact or law), which is the ethical backdrop for source-locking factual assertions in filings.
claims.raw_snippet: ABA Model Rule 3.3: a lawyer shall not knowingly make a false statement of fact or law to a tribunal.

claims.claim: Objective advertising/marketing claims generally require prior substantiation; unsubstantiated performance or comparative claims are a compliance risk, motivating a source-lock pass before publication.
claims.raw_snippet: FTC: objective product claims must be substantiated before they are disseminated.

claims.claim: Direct quotations must match the source verbatim; an altered negation, added qualifier, or meaning-changing ellipsis is a high-severity defect even when the citation is correct.
claims.raw_snippet: Quotations are the strictest type: they must match the source verbatim. A dropped word or an ellipsis that changes meaning is a HIGH-severity defect even when the citation is correct.

claims.claim: The bundled claim_scanner.py is Python stdlib only (no network, no third-party deps) and ships an embedded self-check runnable via --selftest, which passes.
claims.raw_snippet: `python scripts/claim_scanner.py --selftest` prints 'selftest OK'. Verified 2026-07-09 on python3.11. First-pass sentence/citation scanner; does not judge source support.
